messages:
mira: quick heads up — observed requests for tenant 'org-b' landing in default GPU pool even though clients are setting X-Tenant and they have a private endpoint bound. anyone else seeing mismatch?
alex: hmm, that sounds like the matcher is ignoring header hints for private-bound routes. pinging @sam to confirm if the latest matcher PR changed precedence.
sam: yeah, I pushed the matcher tweak two weeks ago to reduce header-based matches because of header-spoofing incidents. prioritized host+path over headers unless we have explicit header provenance. maybe that regressed private endpoint behavior.
pj: are we validating header provenance today? i thought we used token-scoped claims to assert tenant identity. if header is untrusted we should still route by private endpoint mapping.
alex: we do validate token->workspace mapping for API tokens, but some legacy clients call with API key + header. the matcher change tried to avoid accidental hijack when host is wildcard.
olivia: TL;DR: need a deterministic rule for private endpoint + header hints. current problem: private endpoint binding should be authoritative, not optional.
router-bot: match-engine v2.14 deployed to canary on gw-us-2 at 2026-03-16T08:12:30Z — change: header-priority lowered.
deploy-bot: rollout note: canary 10% -> paused due to increased default-pool hits (alert id: ALERT-rt-482).
mira: repro snippet: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer xxxxx" -H "X-Tenant: org-b" 'https://gw.us.redwood/api/v1/generate' -> response debug shows matched_route: default_pool - should match dedicated_pool/org-b.
sam: can you paste the route spec for org-b private endpoint? might be a scoping rule mismatch.
mira: route snippet: ```yaml
id: route-org-b-private
match:
  host: "*.gw.us.redwood"
  path_prefix: "/api/v1"
  headers:
    - name: "X-Tenant"
      value: "org-b"
private_endpoint: true
pool_bind: "dedicated-org-b"
```
alex: ok that config should win. current matcher has a special-case: when private_endpoint=true we still apply "spoof-protection" which deprioritizes header-only matches unless host exactly equals the private endpoint host. that's the regression.
pj: what about requiring a header+token check combo for header-based routing? e.g., header match only accepted if token_claim.workspace==header or TLS client cert present.
olivia: we should avoid breaking clients; better short-term fix is: if route.private_endpoint==true and pool_bind set -> force pool match regardless of header provenance, but record telemetry for mismatches. longer-term: implement token claim enforcement.
sam: agree. quick patch: change matcher precedence order for private_endpoint routes to check pool_bind first, then host/path, then header.
mira: that would fix observed hits. can we add a safeguard: if header != token_claim then log at warn and increment metric tenant.header.mismatch?
alex: yes. I'll open a PR with both changes: precedence tweak + telemetry + warning metric.
router-bot: created issue MATCHER-912: enforce pool_bind precedence for private routes + telemetry.
deploy-bot: planning canary for match-engine v2.15 with fix tomorrow 03/17 02:00 UTC.
pj: also add e2e test: private endpoint + spoofed header should not switch pool. this prevents regressions.
olivia: add new console alert in routing tab: "private-route:header-mismatch-rate" with 5m window. Ops should get paging if >0.5% traffic.
sam: small note — make sure we don't accidentally route multi-tenant hosts that share hostnames. for shared hosts we still fallback to token-claim approach.
mira: thanks all — will monitor canary and send sample traces. appreciate the quick turnaround. :thumbsup:
